requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to actively synchronize its system clock with pool.ntp.org.
requirements.summary: The persistent chrony source was changed to pool.ntp.org, chronyd was active and enabled, and direct observations showed NTP=yes, NTPSynchronized=yes, and chronyd selecting pool.ntp.org sources.

A healthy synchronized baseline was captured, the reboot was acknowledged and produced a bounded connection loss, the boot ID changed, and node1 returned running with the requested configuration, chronyd enabled and active, NTPSynchronized=yes, and a newly selected pool.ntp.org source. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 demonstrably synchronized through chronyd with pool.ntp.org and recovered that configuration and healthy synchronization after a proven reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete and coherent for the sole managed node. Only a minor retained backup-file hygiene issue was identified.
limitations: The backup destination in cmd-6e0f0c6b49964da6 was redacted and /etc was not included in lifecycle file inventories; its retained status is inferred from the successful copy and absence of any cleanup command.
Some chronyc query commands captured no stdout, but direct timedatectl state and chronyd journal selections provided equivalent evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All terminal commands were reviewed. The necessary state changes were the chrony configuration edit, service restart, and scheduled reboot. The only minor unnecessary mutation under the strict hygiene criterion was the extra rollback copy created alongside the configuration edit; no removal is evidenced, so it is treated as retained. It was bounded and low-risk. No failed services, package damage, unsafe socket exposure, or abnormal temporary-file residue was observed after execution.
